name: Naphthalene

energies.comment: Two fused aromatic rings. Calculated from NIST: ΔHf = 150 ± 10 kJ/mol → BDE = (10×716.68 + 8×218.0) - 150 = 8761 kJ/mol. Naive Kekulé sum (5 C=C, 6 C-C, 8 C-H) = 8390 kJ/mol → violation +371 ± 10 kJ/mol. Naphthalene/benzene = 371/203 = 1.83×, i.e. ~0.91× per ring. The earlier +115 figure (and the 'diminishing returns, 0.78× per ring' claim) came from a naive-model bug that assigned 6 C=C bonds, which is not a valid Kekulé structure. See docs/Claude-Reasoning/020.
energies.source: Thermodynamics Research Center, 1997 (average of 7 values); NIST Chemistry WebBook
energies.confidence_note: NIST-verified value from average of 7 experimental measurements. Larger uncertainty (±10 kJ/mol) reflects variation between methods.

reference_energies.comment: Standard bond energies for naive calculation

notes: Naphthalene: two fused benzene rings sharing one C-C edge
Violation vs mean-bond-enthalpy Kekulé baseline: +371 ± 10 kJ/mol
Ratio to benzene (+203): 1.83×, ~0.91× per ring — slightly sub-linear, within what baseline error could produce
Previous +115 / 0.78× 'diminishing returns' finding was an artifact of an invalid Kekulé assignment (6 C=C instead of 5)
Tests: How does aromatic stabilization scale with ring count? Needs a better baseline (homodesmotic / group additivity) before interpreting
